desc: On 23 February 2026, at a stop on his 'Arsenal of Freedom' tour in Louisville, Colorado - four days after the President's Truth Social direction - Secretary of War Pete Hegseth committed the Department to UAP disclosure in terms that have shaped everything since. He said the Department would 'be in full compliance with that executive order, [and we're] eager to provide that for the president. So, there'll be more coming on that,' and that 'We've got our people working on it right now...we're digging in.' He characterised the President as 'just committed to disclosure on lots of levels' and warned that 'It'll be a deliberative process' and 'I don't want to over-promise and under-deliver. So, we're going to take a little time.' The phrase 'that executive order' is the crux: no signed executive order on UAP declassification has appeared in the public record, and the contemporaneous reporting describes a social-media post. Either the Secretary of War mischaracterised a Truth Social post as an executive order in public, or an unpublished order exists. In the same reporting Pentagon spokesperson Sue Gough confirmed AARO had examined over 2,000 UAP cases, with approximately 1,000 reports lacking sufficient data held in an Active Archive - growth of at least 400 cases since late 2024. Jordan Flowers of the Disclosure Foundation urged expedited release of unclassified material and warned against 'misleadingly partial or incomplete disclosures.'
